scenes.chapter: Chapter 1  A line on the bus
lines: Back then, the front seats were for white riders only,
and Black riders had to sit in the back.
Parks, forty-two, was a seamstress
and the secretary of the local NAACP.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 2  She did not stand up
lines: That evening, after work, she sat in the first row of the Black section.
As the bus filled, the driver told her and three others to move;
the other three stood up, but she did not.
Later she said she was not tired in body, but tired of giving in,
and she was arrested on the spot.
The news spread; Black residents quit the buses.

Her question for you:
When a rule is unfair, would you dare to say no?
